reason: The 1986 Berlin nosology is the foundational clinical classification framework for heritable connective tissue disorders, including Marfan syndrome, which is caused by FBN1 mutations. As an essential reference document for understanding the disease phenotype that FBN1 mutations produce, it belongs in the FBN1 collection. The absence of an abstract is expected for a nosology/classification paper from 1986.

The paper is about the role of AP-2beta (TFAP2B) in trabecular meshwork development, Schlemm's canal formation, and intraocular pressure homeostasis. These are glaucoma/aqueous outflow pathway topics. 'Transparent media' in ophthalmology anatomy refers to the optically clear structures light passes through (cornea, aqueous humor, lens, vitreous); this paper studies IOP regulation mechanisms and outflow pathway structures, not the anatomy or optical properties of transparent media. The connection to 'Transparent media' is too indirect to justify inclusion.

This paper specifically recapitulates the vascular (aortic) aspect of Marfan syndrome by targeting FBN1 (fibrillin-1). ADAMTSL4 mutations cause autosomal recessive isolated ectopia lentis, not aortic or cardiovascular disease. The paper has an empty abstract and its title frames it exclusively as an FBN1/vascular-Marfan study. There is no plausible route by which a paper about the aortic phenotype of FBN1 knockout is specifically relevant to ADAMTSL4 biology.

This review covers fibrillin-1 structure, assembly, and the role of FBN1 mutations in fibrillinopathies. It is directly relevant to FBN1. It is also relevant to ADAMTSL4 because ADAMTSL4 functions within the fibrillin-1 microfibril system, and this review provides essential mechanistic context for understanding how disruption of that system causes ectopia lentis. The score of 5 against a threshold of 6 is marginal and does not outweigh the clear topical relevance.

The title describes a general study of ubiquitin's role in spliceosome assembly. The abstract is empty, providing no evidence that the paper specifically addresses DHX38 (PRPF16) or SNRNP200 (U5-200KD/Brr2). Although both genes are spliceosome components, a broad paper on ubiquitin and spliceosome assembly is not specifically about these RP-associated helicases. The score-below-threshold rejection is appropriate absent evidence of direct relevance.
Classic 1991 Nature paper establishing genetic linkage of Marfan syndrome to two fibrillin genes, one of which is FBN1 on chromosome 15. This is a foundational genetics paper for the FBN1 collection.

Directly studies fibrillin transcript from a Marfan syndrome patient and demonstrates nonsense-mutation-induced exon skipping in FBN1. The abstract explicitly mentions fibrillin and Marfan syndrome, making this a core FBN1 disease-mechanism paper.
Maps the Marfan syndrome genetic defect to chromosome 15 (where FBN1 resides) using linkage analysis. Foundational paper in the discovery of FBN1 as the Marfan gene. Directly relevant to FBN1.

Studies fibrillin (FBN1 protein) synthesis, secretion, and extracellular matrix incorporation in dermal fibroblasts from 26 Marfan syndrome probands. Directly confirms FBN1 as the Marfan gene and characterizes the range of biochemical defects. Core FBN1 biology paper.

Reports three new FBN1 missense mutations in Marfan syndrome patients, all in EGF-like domains at cysteine residues. The abstract explicitly names FBN1 and characterizes its mutations in Marfan syndrome. Directly on-topic.

Prospectively evaluates 279 patients referred for suspected Marfan syndrome to characterize the spectrum of Marfan-like features and differential diagnoses. FBN1 is the defining gene for Marfan syndrome; this clinical characterization study is directly relevant to the FBN1 collection.

Describes a software package and database for analysis of FBN1 mutations in Marfan syndrome. The abstract explicitly names FBN1, Marfan syndrome, and the database contents. Directly relevant to FBN1 mutation analysis.

Title explicitly states that mutations at the 3' end of the FBN1 gene cause the neonatal progeroid variant of Marfan syndrome with congenital lipodystrophy. Directly about FBN1 genotype-phenotype correlation. Relevant despite empty abstract.

Evaluates diagnostic utility of FBN1 genotype combined with Ghent nosology phenotype in 300 consecutive patients referred for Marfan syndrome. The abstract explicitly discusses FBN1 mutation status and its effect on diagnosis. Core FBN1 clinical genetics paper.
Second edition of the computerized FBN1 mutation database (89 entries), directly providing mutation analysis tools and data for FBN1 and Marfan syndrome. Directly relevant.

Describes a novel FBN1 missense mutation in a family with a Marfan/ectopia lentis phenotype. The abstract explicitly discusses ectopia lentis (a key ocular manifestation), FBN1, and the fibrillin polypeptide. Directly relevant to both FBN1 and its ocular phenotype.

Title describes compound-heterozygous Marfan syndrome; Marfan syndrome is caused exclusively by FBN1 mutations. A paper about compound-heterozygous Marfan syndrome concerns FBN1 genotype and is directly relevant to the FBN1 collection. Abstract is empty but the title is unambiguous.

Characterizes large genomic deletions in the FBN1 gene using MLPA in Marfan syndrome patients. The abstract explicitly names FBN1, Marfan syndrome, and reports novel FBN1 deletions. Directly relevant.
Title explicitly names an FBN1 mutation causing Marfan-like manifestations via germline mosaicism. Directly relevant to FBN1 genetics despite empty abstract.

Applies dHPLC for mutation detection of the fibrillin-1 (FBN1) gene in 262 patients with Marfan syndrome or Marfan-like phenotypes. The abstract explicitly names FBN1, reports 93 mutations, and demonstrates diagnostic utility. Directly relevant to FBN1.
